identity.name: Acetylated distarch phosphate
identity.chemical_class: Chemically modified starch (acetylated, phosphate-crosslinked starch ester)

function.mechanism: Produced by esterification/crosslinking of food starch (e.g., with sodium trimetaphosphate or phosphorus oxychloride) plus acetylation (acetic anhydride or vinyl acetate), yielding altered viscosity and processing stability.

adi.basis: EFSA re-evaluation concluded no need for a numerical ADI (ADI not specified context for modified starches).

efsa.key_finding: EFSA concluded no safety concern for modified starches (including E1414) at reported uses and use levels in the general population.

fda.notes: Regulated as food starch-modified under direct food additive regulation; section includes reagent/residual limits and states it may be safely used in food under listed conditions.

adi.basis: JECFA chemical page lists ADI as NOT SPECIFIED (2016 entry); 2018 entry is specification-only.

concerns.summary: A 1982 rat study with high dietary inclusion reported caecal enlargement and increased nephrocalcinosis/mineralization markers; authors noted potential dietary mineral-balance confounding and effects were less marked than lactose comparator.
EFSA reports modified starches are not absorbed intact and are hydrolyzed/fermented; this indicates GI processing effects but not a demonstrated safety signal at approved uses.
Recent PubMed records are largely food-technology functionality studies rather than modern chronic toxicology or epidemiology specific to E1414.
key_references: PubMed query: acetylated distarch phosphate OR E1414 (accessed 2026-02-27)

no_concern_confirmed: EFSA 2017: no safety concern at reported uses/use levels; no need for numerical ADI for modified starch group including E1414.
JECFA database: ADI NOT SPECIFIED entries for acetylated distarch phosphate.
IARC classification dataset search found no listing for acetylated distarch phosphate/E1414.

adi_exceedance.notes: EFSA/JECFA use non-numerical ADI framing (not specified), so numerical ADI exceedance cannot be computed directly for E1414. EFSA reported group-level modified starch exposure estimates.

risk_assessment.rationale: Authoritative regulators (EFSA/JECFA/FDA-CFR framework) support continued use with no numerical ADI requirement in the modified starch context, while additive-specific modern long-term toxicology evidence is limited and older high-dose animal findings remain of uncertain human relevance.
key_factors: EFSA 2017 no-safety-concern conclusion for modified starches including E1414
JECFA ADI listed as NOT SPECIFIED (latest toxicological entry 2016; 2018 specification-only)
US regulation under 21 CFR 172.892 with explicit reagent/limit conditions
No IARC listing identified for this agent
Sparse modern E1414-specific chronic human safety data
